text:
marta: Heads-up — I’m seeing a sustained p99 CPU jump on telemetry-collector after the canary landed (~10:15 UTC). spans/sec up ~3x and exporter threads look saturated. :thinking:

alex: saw it too. graph shows a big fat tail starting at 10:12. can you paste the collector logs?

marta: pasted a short excerpt: 
```
2026-03-18T10:13:02Z collector INFO exporter_fallback: route fallthrough to https://exporter-legacy:4317
2026-03-18T10:13:03Z collector WARN batching: queueing_delay_ms=1200 enqueued=2048
2026-03-18T10:13:05Z collector DEBUG exporter_client: send_batch size=4096 bytes=12.3MB duration_ms=2400
2026-03-18T10:13:06Z collector INFO cpu_usage_pct=93 p95_ms=1200 p99_ms=3800
```

suri: that send_batch size=4096 is a red flag — looks like we’re pushing huge batches to the legacy exporter which is single-threaded.

jun: is this the fallthrough path we added to route to legacy when grpc connection fails? Could be retry/backoff not kicking in.

marta: correct — routing policy now tries primary -> fallback, but fallback has no concurrency limits set. When primary had transient errors, collector queued everything and then fell through.

alex: quick mitigation: reduce max_batch_size + set exporter concurrency=4 for legacy. Suggest patch: 
```
exporters:
  legacy:
    endpoint: https://exporter-legacy:4317
    max_batch_size: 512
    max_concurrent_requests: 4
    retry:
      enabled: true
      initial_backoff_ms: 100
      max_backoff_ms: 2000
```

suri: also enable per-exporter circuit breaker so we don’t amplify load to a slow endpoint. something like `circuit_breaker: {failure_threshold: 5, cooldown_ms: 60000}`

deploy-bot: canary-deploy started by jun — rollout id: r-2026-03-18-312.

jun: I’ll roll the canary back for the legacy-fallback policy while we validate config changes.

marta: thanks. before rollback I want to capture a profiler snapshot to see where time is spent (KV cache, serialization, or exporter blocking). Running `curl http://collector/metrics` now.

alex: profiler output looked like serializer + http client wait. attaching a tiny flame: serialization ~35%, http wait ~50%, runtime GC ~10%.

suri: GC 10% might indicate huge allocations from the batch aggregator — big batches -> big byte arrays. switching to streaming marshal might help. but that’s a bit invasive.

jun: immediate ops plan: 1) rollback canary; 2) patch exporter config to limit batch size and concurrency; 3) add circuit breaker + backoff; 4) enable a temporary sampling throttle for debug traces to reduce spans/sec by 5x, preserve infra traces only.

marta: agree. can we do sampling throttle via runtime flag without a redeploy? I think collector supports a dynamic config endpoint.

alex: yes — pushing dynamic config now: `patch /config/dynamic -> sampling.trace_rate=0.2`

deploy-bot: canary-deploy rollback triggered by jun — rollout id r-2026-03-18-312 — status: in_progress.

marta: after throttle, CPU dropped to p99 45% within 90s. spans/sec back to baseline. Good signal that volume -> batching amplification was the main cause.

suri: follow-ups for an actual fix: - default max_batch_size to 1024 or lower - enforce per-exporter concurrency - add exporter-level queue-length soft limits with shedding - add telemetry of exporter queue lengths to console dashboard

alex: also add a unit/integration test for fallthrough scenario: simulate primary failing, ensure fallback has concurrency/backoff and that overall p99 stays under threshold.

jun: I’ll open a quick PR for config defaults and the circuit breaker, and a follow-up story for streaming marshalling.

marta: filing the incident ticket with timeline & metrics now. tagging @suri @alex for reviews.

suri: :thumbsup: Also adding a dashboard panel: `telemetry.collector.exporter_queue_length{exporter=legacy}` with p50/p95/p99.

alex: can we add an automated alert: if exporter_queue_length.p99 > 200 for 5m, page eng-platform?

marta: yes — add to alerts repo.

deploy-bot: canary rollback completed — rollout id r-2026-03-18-312 — status: success.

jun: postmortem action items added to ticket: CONFIG-342, PERF-119, DASH-58.

marta: great work team. I’ll attach profiler and the sampling-change diff to the incident ticket.
